record.title: Kharlachi COVID goods restriction, March–July 2020
record.direction: Both directions or unspecified in the reports
record.exceptions: Other Pakistan–Afghanistan crossings reopened earlier; their dates do not set this post’s dates. Passenger scope remains outside the phase.
record.enforcement: Named-post onset and continuing trade restriction in June; independent-publisher official-attribution report and same-publisher local account of actual July 11 trade restoration.
record.record_type: Crossing-specific episode or qualified restriction observations
record.relationship: No matching episode in the 754-parent compact inventory or screened pending additions. Shared national measures are not duplicated by post.
record.status_observation: Historical scoped evidence only; no openness or closure is inferred after the supported observations.
record.current_corrections: 118 calendar-day difference for the reported Kharlachi goods restriction from 15 March to 11 July 2020. March 15 comes from a retrospective named-trader account, supported by continuing June restriction and July reopening reports; it is not imported from another crossing. No passenger endpoint or measured elapsed-hour precision is claimed.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: The restriction is explicitly reported as a COVID containment measure; later traders’ livelihood complaints are consequences, not an additional closure rationale.
